comparator.name: Future Planet Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum defines a 180-EC programme with 60 EC in each year. Year 1 is a compulsory shared programme in climate and energy, quality of life, Earth and social systems, environmental economics, hazards, data and research. In Year 2 every student follows 15 EC of shared philosophy, scenario-planning and food-forestry study plus one 45-EC major. The normalized target is the generic bachelor; Future Earth and Future Society are equally formal specialisations, and neither is identified as the general route. Future Earth is therefore selected by its first-listed position in the current official curriculum, independently of UCR fit. Its 45 EC combines Earth science, biology and chemistry through plant-soil study, food and ecosystems, remote sensing, R programming, statistics, digital Earth, aquatic systems, water management and desertification fieldwork. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine open choice, followed by the 6-EC Future Planet Project, 6-EC Research Designs and an 18-EC major-specific Bachelor Project. The official February 2026 curriculum chart confirms these components and credits for 2026-2027.

alternatives.label: Earth systems, food & water sustainability
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible response to the selected Future Earth route: an integrated sustainability programme centred on Earth systems, climate, ecosystems, soils, sustainable food and water, while retaining economics, governance and environmental justice. Mathematical, statistical, spatial and field methods support evidence-based environmental research.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the selected Future Earth route through Earth systems, ecology, soils, food, water and environmental research while retaining the programme's shared societal dimension.
progression: Sustainability, Earth-system, ecology, economics and methods foundations precede spatial analysis, soil and water study, upper-level environmental science, statistics, governance and partner-facing research; prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort offerings pass.
traceOverrides: examines circular resource use, recovery and remediation within an integrated sustainability programme
examines resource and environmental challenges through advanced Earth-system research

alternatives.label: Future Society: governance & just transitions
alternatives.concept: Develops the programme's official Future Society direction through environmental governance, political institutions, law, economics, justice, climate communication and stakeholder action, grounded in climate, Earth systems, spatial data and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.labelReason: The official Future Society direction supplies the organising logic; governance, politics, law, environmental justice and climate communication form the scheduled focus.
progression: Sustainability, law, politics, economics, research and data foundations precede international law, public economics, advanced EU politics, governance, conflict analysis and applied sustainability research; prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort offerings pass.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ecology, hazards, soils, sustainable farming and advanced quantitative depth with a sequenced law, politics, justice and communication curriculum. The programmes differ by eight courses and 60 EC in each direction.
traceOverrides: examines circular resource use, recovery and remediation as a sustainability-governance problem
provides advanced Earth-resource evidence for environmental governance decisions

alternatives.label: Sustainable enterprise, energy & resources
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced energy-transition, green-building and environmental-enterprise direction by linking renewable-system design, resource geoscience and circular material flows to business models, economics, organisational change and governance. Data, research and environmental media place enterprise decisions in their wider planetary context.
alternatives.labelReason: Enterprise, innovation and leadership are combined with a sequenced energy, resource and circular-economy curriculum supported by explicit programme topics and outcomes.
progression: Business, sustainability, economics, methods and Earth-science foundations precede public economics, energy design, resource research, leadership, econometrics and international business governance; prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort offerings pass.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes entrepreneurship, circularity, renewable-system design, organisational innovation and international business for the closest route's ecology, hazards, soil-water management and advanced mathematical emphasis. It differs from the closest route by eight courses and 60 EC in each direction and from the governance route by nine courses and 67.5 EC in each direction.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has two equally formal majors, Future Earth and Future Society. Neither is identified as broader, less specialised or more representative of the overall bachelor, so the first-listed Future Earth major is selected from the current official 2026-2027 curriculum before considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: After the closest Future Earth-informed programme, the official Future Society major supports a distinct governance-and-justice alternative, and the explicit energy-transition, green-building and environmental-enterprise evidence supports a third programme. All three are coherent, feasible and exceed the 30-EC pairwise course-difference floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Earth systems, climate, ecosystems, food and water
Both introduce complex sustainability challenges and systems thinking; the UvA course includes a first academic paper.
Both introduce geological, chemical and biological Earth-system processes.
Both examine climate-system processes, impacts, sea-level change and societal responses.
Both address ecosystems and biodiversity; the UvA course connects global biomes explicitly to food supply.
Both analyse spatial patterns of environmental hazards and adaptation; the UvA course uses Google Earth Pro.
Both develop remote-sensing and spatial-data methods for environmental change.
Both study soil properties and their environmental significance; the UvA course focuses specifically on plant-soil relations in food systems.
Both critically examine sustainable alternatives to industrial agriculture.
Both study water availability, hydrological processes, management and adaptation.
The compulsory Future Earth laboratory and field practical has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The dedicated aquatic-science and aquatic-ecosystem course has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The preparatory environmental-data course tied to the Desertification field course has no separate UCR equivalent.
The dedicated field course in geo-ecological mapping and desertification has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
Both develop future-oriented responses to coupled human-environment problems; the UvA course teaches formal complexity-based scenario planning.
Both examine how science, politics, institutions and society shape sustainability transitions.
Both examine human-nature conflict and environmental justice; the UvA course frames these questions through quality of life.
Both introduce economic systems, environmental externalities and responses to environmental problems.
Both compare energy sources and transitions through technical, economic and environmental perspectives.
Data, research, projects and open space
Both teach research design and quantitative methods; the UvA course directly scaffolds the parallel Bachelor Project.
Both introduce data processing, visualisation and statistical analysis for applied research.
Both develop statistical models, uncertainty estimation and hypothesis testing.
Both are collaborative sustainability research projects addressing complex real-world environmental problems.
The dedicated group research course combining interviews and surveys around quality of life has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The compulsory programme-specific philosophy-of-science course has no single course in these UCR schedules.
The dedicated R programming course has no separate ordinary-course equivalent in these UCR schedules.
The genuine 30-EC elective semester remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.
The compulsory 18-EC individual Bachelor Project cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or as UCR's optional comparison-only research element.

notes.text: UvA organises Future Planet Studies around semester challenges, a formal 45-EC Future Earth major, dedicated R and spatial-methods courses, field and laboratory practicals, and an 18-EC Bachelor Project. UCR can construct coherent programmes across the same broad environmental and societal territory, but it distributes that study across separate courses rather than reproducing UvA's integrated challenge sequence and major structure.
